booking-engine.Admin Portal: resource configuration and booking management/approvals (FR-029, FR-053, FR-054)
booking-engine.Booking Engine: slots, rules, approval flow, cancellation windows (BR-002..BR-005)

laundry.Admin Portal: staff act on and progress orders manually; laundry catalogue (FR-066, FR-055)
laundry.Service Orders: laundry orders against configurable catalogue and lifecycle
laundry.Notification Dispatcher: order status updates reach the resident (core loop: resident receives status updates)
laundry.Payment Module: order paid where online payment applies (FR-030, ServiceOrder->Payment in §8)

key_changes: Added Payment Module to booking-engine and laundry after both sets linked it: FR-070 and FR-030 make payment part of confirming those orders, and §8 links Booking and ServiceOrder to Payment, so the payable-subject wiring is real work in the Payment Module, not only in the separate payments feature.

X_wrong_reasons.Admin and Reporting: dashboard tiles and report counts (FR-050, FR-061) are a separate admin-reporting feature; the client feature works without them, so linking claims reporting work inside each feature
X_wrong_reasons.PostgreSQL Database: the DB is a managed instance / system of record; ordinary tables and migrations belong to the owning backend component (C4: <component> -> db 'persists ...'). Only booking-engine earns a DB link, for the range-exclusion invariant
X_wrong_reasons.Admin Portal (payments): no in-scope FR asks for an admin transaction view or staff-triggered refunds; §6 Admin Portal responsibility lists no payment screens - the why is invented scope

patterns: X links PostgreSQL Database to every feature for 'tables must be added', treating routine schema work owned by each backend component as DB-component work (5 wrong); Y links the DB only where a DB-layer invariant (range exclusion) is the work.
X links Admin and Reporting wherever a dashboard tile or report count mentions the feature, claiming reporting work the feature does not need to function (4 wrong).
X invents scope from a plausible need not in requirements (Admin Portal refunds/transaction view for payments).
Neither set missed a needed link; both correctly pulled Payment Module into booking and laundry, which corrected the judge's key.
